project.title: WePresent No. 5
project.maker: Paula Scher and team at Pentagram for WeTransfer / WePresent
project.format: A community-focused issue of WeTransfer's arts and editorial platform, released in three localized design variants for New York, Amman, and Berlin

why: A strong editorial-system reference because a shared community brief yields three local editions rather than one universal visual answer: the New York edition turns a neighborhood walk into a map-led entry point, while its typographic range makes the issue feel specific without losing the parent publication's identity.

readingRhythm.title: A local walk becomes the issue's narrative doorway
readingRhythm.study: Pentagram's case study describes Paula Scher's map of Mimi's morning walk through NoMad as the New York edition's response to the issue's neighborhood and community theme.
readingRhythm.reuse: Use an original route, field note, or local index as an editorial entry device when a theme needs to feel grounded in a particular place.

readingRhythm.title: One editorial brief, three distinct local versions
readingRhythm.study: WePresent No. 5 was created by separate designers in New York, Amman, and Berlin, making regional interpretation part of the publication structure rather than an afterthought.
readingRhythm.reuse: Define the shared editorial question and a small set of fixed production constraints, then allow local makers to answer it with distinct content and visual decisions.

compositions.title: Map-as-feature composition
compositions.study: The NoMad walking map makes a route, its landmarks, and the magazine's cover character operate as one feature concept rather than as separate decorative elements.
compositions.reuse: Let a map provide both navigational logic and visual hierarchy when an editorial story is rooted in a specific place; redraw every mark and route from original research.

compositions.title: A single character creates an approachable cover anchor
compositions.study: The case study presents Mimi as the cover star and repeats the character in the community-focused editorial material, joining cover and interior through a simple narrative device.
compositions.reuse: Choose an original recurring subject when a publication needs a warm, memorable bridge from cover to feature without copying a source character or image.

typeImageSystems.role: A playful voice across cover and feature material
typeImageSystems.notes: Pentagram identifies enlarged Helvetica, Megazoid, Calcula, and hand-lettering as part of the edition's typographic play.
typeImageSystems.reuse: Mix a stable utilitarian text face with one or two expressive display roles only after establishing clear hierarchy; license or substitute all typefaces appropriately.

assets.role: Regional interpretation within a shared issue
assets.notes: The three city editions use different design teams under the same neighborhood and community brief. Their artwork, lettering, map, and imagery remain external source material and are not included here.
assets.reuse: Specify shared editorial constraints before commissioning localized editions, then preserve space for each team to make genuinely local choices.

assets.role: Display variation without abandoning editorial order
assets.notes: The source documents several named type treatments and hand lettering; the local shared preview uses only its existing original CSS and system-font approach.
assets.reuse: Prototype typographic contrast with original copy, licensed fonts, and neutral geometry instead of recreating a source publication's artwork or lettering.

implementation.format: Localized print editorial issue using map-led narrative structure, a cover character, and layered typographic roles
implementation.notes: Pentagram's first-party case study explicitly documents the print-publication context, the three-city edition model, the NoMad map, the cover role, and the typographic ingredients. No source artwork, DALL-E imagery, map, dog image, lettering, or publication files are copied into this library.
